family.shared_definition: a licensed public passenger vehicle for hire with a driver
family.neutral_stem: The traveler hurried out of the terminal and hailed the
family.semantic_notes: 'Taxi' is internationally universal, whereas 'cab' is slightly more colloquial and strongly associated with major metropolitan cities.

source_context_dev: Arriving during peak surge pricing meant ground transport fares were through the roof. Still, desperate to avoid the downpour, a ride was needed immediately.
The city center was in gridlock and rates had quadrupled across every curbside transit rank. Money was no object given the looming business deadline.
Premium airport surcharges were in full effect, doubling the usual cost of citybound transit. With no patience left for waiting, standard budgetary limits were ignored.
Stepping outside into the biting cold, high-end private dispatch services were demanding exorbitant fees. The urgent rush to make dinner left no room to bargain.

The curbside concourse was quiet past midnight, offering dozens of vacant vehicles lined along the curb. Spotting an unoccupied ride was effortless.
After deboarding, the queue outside was moving fast as plenty of open automobiles pulled up one after another. Finding a vehicle with no current passengers was simple.
The terminal exit was breezy and uncrowded, with numerous waiting operators seeking their next fare. An unreserved vehicle was waiting right near the crosswalk.

Few travelers were lingering outside, leaving plenty of unoccupied transport options lined up along the boulevard. A vehicle ready for immediate boarding stood nearby.
